title: Molar-flow basis conversion
purpose: Convert the 100 kmol/h assumed process throughput to mol/s for EOS volumetric flow calculations.
data: F = 100 kmol/h; 1 kmol = 1000 mol; 1 h = 3600 s.
interpretation: Use SI molar flow in volumetric-flow and thermodynamic equations; preserve kmol/h for stream reporting.
assumptions: Throughput is a process-scale assumption rather than experimental metadata.

title: Feed composition normalization
purpose: Check that the specified feed composition is physically normalized.
interpretation: Normalized input satisfies the binary feed composition constraint.
assumptions: No analytical composition uncertainty was supplied for the assumed feed.

title: Feed component molar rates
purpose: Determine feed molar rate of each component.
interpretation: The design basis contains equal molar feed rates.
assumptions: Assumed feed rate and composition.

title: Mixture molecular weight in feed
purpose: Convert the feed to a mass basis.
interpretation: An equimolar mixture is ethanol-rich by mass because ethanol has the larger molecular weight.
verification: Weighted average is within pure-component endpoints.
assumptions: Uses CoolProp/NIST component molecular weights as listed in the property register.

title: Feed mass flow by component
purpose: Calculate feed mass flows and total mass flow.
data: n_i = 50 kmol/h each; MW_E=46.06844; MW_W=18.015268 kg/kmol.
interpretation: The mass feed is dominated by ethanol, although molar feed is equimolar.
assumptions: Feed basis is an assumed 100 kmol/h.

title: Experimental tie-line interpolation
purpose: Interpolate liquid/vapour ethanol composition at selected T on 1.5 MPa isobar.
interpretation: The reference tie-line is interpolated only within the measured 1.5 MPa data interval.
verification: Both compositions lie inside adjacent experimental points; no extrapolation.
assumptions: The interpolation defines a reference fixture, not an EOS prediction.

title: Complementary mole fractions
purpose: Obtain water compositions by mole-fraction closure.
interpretation: Binary compositions close exactly by construction.
assumptions: Reported precision should not imply more accuracy than Table 6.

title: Lever-rule vapour fraction
purpose: Calculate the empirical flash vapour fraction for the specified feed composition.
interpretation: Approximately 69.8 mol% of the feed appears in the vapour reference stream.
assumptions: Valid for the reference tie-line and overall material balance; not the rejected NRTL-SRK flash.

title: Liquid and vapour total rates
purpose: Determine total phase rates from feed and vapour fraction.
interpretation: The phase flow rates sum to the feed rate.
assumptions: Based on empirical interpolation.

title: Component split rates
purpose: Calculate each component flow in each phase.
interpretation: Vapour stream is enriched in ethanol relative to the liquid at this measured tie-line.
verification: Each feed component recovered across both outlets.
assumptions: Composition and phase amount inherited from empirical tie-line.

title: Component molar closure
purpose: Verify the component material balances.
data: Feed 50 kmol/h each; outlet flows from MC-010.
interpretation: No component accumulation is assumed at steady state.
verification: Exact within double-precision arithmetic of the lever-rule calculation.
assumptions: No reaction, leak or purge included.

title: Total molar closure
purpose: Verify overall total flow.
interpretation: Total material balance is satisfied algebraically.
assumptions: This is a calculated closure check, not an experimental validation.

title: Mass balance closure
purpose: Verify mass closure using molecular weights.
data: Feed component mass rates=2303.422 and 900.7634 kg/h; outlet phase flows calculated from n×MW.
interpretation: Mass closure is consistent with component molar closure.
assumptions: No component transformations or material loss modeled.

title: Ethanol recovery to vapour
purpose: Quantify fraction of feed ethanol recovered in vapour outlet.
interpretation: This is a vapour-phase distribution metric, not finished-product purity or process yield.
assumptions: Empirical phase split only.

title: Water recovery to vapour
purpose: Quantify water distribution to vapour outlet.
interpretation: Vapour stream contains significant water; this is not a dehydration process.
assumptions: Empirical phase split only.

title: Apparent equilibrium ratios
purpose: Compute K values from measured phase compositions.
interpretation: Apparent K values indicate ethanol favoured in vapour at this tie-line.
verification: K values are finite and positive.
assumptions: These are empirical apparent K values, not model-based calculated K from NRTL-SRK.

title: Relative volatility
purpose: Calculate relative volatility from apparent K values.
interpretation: Ethanol/water has a relative volatility above unity at this state, but azeotropic constraints vary with pressure.
assumptions: Local apparent value only.

title: Ethanol saturation pressure
purpose: Evaluate NIST Antoine equation.
interpretation: Calculated Psat is slightly above total pressure, showing why this near-critical/high pressure state must use fugacity/reference corrections rather than a naive low-pressure formula.
verification: T lies within NIST correlation range.
assumptions: Pure-component saturation correlation; no mixture VLE is inferred directly.

title: Water saturation pressure
purpose: Evaluate NIST Antoine equation with pressure output in bar.
interpretation: Water saturation pressure is materially below operating pressure.
verification: T lies within NIST correlation range.
assumptions: Do not use coefficients in the atm form with bar conversion omitted.

title: Saturation-pressure ratios
purpose: Compare system pressure to pure saturation pressures.
data: P=15 bar; Psat_E=15.4177988 bar; Psat_W=8.99893704 bar.
interpretation: This highlights strong pressure effects and the importance of careful fugacity treatment.
verification: Calculated from a consistent bar basis.
assumptions: Do not infer phase stability from this ratio alone.

title: NRTL τ and G matrices
purpose: Calculate candidate NRTL interaction quantities.
interpretation: The asymmetry of τ12 and τ21 is explicit.
verification: Recalculated with component order ethanol=1, water=2.
assumptions: Candidate low-pressure parameter set; not accepted at high pressure.

title: NRTL activity coefficients
purpose: Evaluate NRTL logarithmic activity coefficients at empirical liquid composition.
equation: lnγ_i=Σ_j x_jτ_jiG_ji/Σ_k x_kG_ki + Σ_j x_jG_ij/Σ_k x_kG_kj(τ_ij−Σ_m x_mτ_mjG_mj/Σ_k x_kG_kj)
substitution: Substitute x, τ, G in the full two-component sums; retain both asymmetric pair directions.
interpretation: The calculated liquid phase is non-ideal under the candidate set.
verification: γ_i>0 and limiting ideal pure-component cases follow algebraically; high-pressure data fit still fails.
assumptions: No use as validated activity coefficient at 445 K.

title: SRK pure-component parameters
purpose: Calculate classical SRK m, alpha, a_i and b_i using sourced Tc/Pc/omega.
substitution: Evaluate each component independently in SI.
result: Pure SRK parameters exported in intermediate thermodynamic CSV.
unit: SI: a in Pa·m6/mol2, b in m3/mol
interpretation: Source-frozen pure properties allow reproducibility, but mixing rules and kij still require validation.
assumptions: Classical Soave alpha form.

title: SRK mixture A and B
purpose: Calculate SRK dimensionless parameters for vapour composition.
equation: a_m=ΣΣ y_i y_j√(a_i a_j)(1−kij); b_m=Σy_i b_i; A=a_mP/(R²T²); B=b_mP/(RT)
substitution: Use a_i,b_i from MC-023 and specified y.
interpretation: The cubic EOS is evaluated at the measured vapour composition.
assumptions: Diagnostic SRK parameters, not accepted model outputs.

title: SRK cubic roots and vapour-root selection
purpose: Solve the SRK compressibility cubic and select the admissible vapour root.
data: Equation Z³−Z²+(A−B−B²)Z−AB=0 with A/B from MC-024.
equation: Roots of cubic; admissible Z>B; vapour root is largest real root above B.
substitution: Solve polynomial and retain all real roots for diagnostics.
result: With source-frozen Tc/Pc/ω roots approximately 0.02569, 0.09432, 0.87999; selected vapour Z≈0.87999
interpretation: Root selection is a numerical phase-root convention only, not a phase-stability test.
verification: Each returned root is checked for imaginary component and Z>B.
assumptions: No tangent-plane stability test is implemented.

title: Vapour fugacity coefficients
purpose: Calculate SRK vapour φ values from the selected root.
data: SRK mix params, y and Z from MC-025.
substitution: Evaluate for ethanol and water; then exponentiate.
interpretation: Vapour nonideality is material; φ differs from unity.
assumptions: Diagnostic only due unaccepted kij and model parameter set.

title: Poynting correction factors
purpose: Calculate pressure correction from saturation pressure to system pressure.
substitution: Apply component-specific vL_i and same SI pressure units.
interpretation: The correction is small for the assumed volumes, but still retained for consistency.
assumptions: Modified-Rackett pure-volume proxies are unvalidated at the design state.

title: Fugacity residual at reference tie-line
purpose: Test target NRTL-SRK fugacity equality independently.
equation: r_i=ln(y_i φ_i^V P /(x_i γ_i Psat_i φ_i^sat Π_i))
substitution: Source-frozen critical properties and candidate NRTL set; kij=0.
interpretation: The residuals greatly exceed the 1×10⁻⁶ criterion; the NRTL-SRK state is rejected.
assumptions: Not a measured error. It diagnoses incompatibility between candidate model and experimental tie-line.

title: Vapour density screening
purpose: Estimate vapour density from ideal-gas compressibility correction.
interpretation: Density is only for preliminary hydraulic sizing.
assumptions: Uses diagnostic SRK Z and empirical composition.

title: Liquid density screening
purpose: Estimate mixture liquid density from composition-weighted molar volume.
interpretation: This ignores excess volume and compressed-liquid effects.
verification: Positive molar volume; mixture density physically plausible as screening only.
assumptions: Modified-Rackett pure volume values are candidate assumptions.

title: Vapour volumetric flow
purpose: Convert vapour molar flow to volumetric flow using SRK Z.
interpretation: Approx. 151.56 m³/h vapour load.
assumptions: Uses rejected diagnostic SRK model; replace with accepted EOS or trusted density.

title: Liquid volumetric flow
purpose: Convert liquid molar flow to volumetric flow.
interpretation: Approximately 1.290 m³/h liquid load.
assumptions: Liquid molar volume approximate.

title: Souders–Brown allowable superficial velocity
purpose: Estimate initial gas capacity for vertical mesh-demister flow.
data: K=0.11 m/s (GPSA comparison value); ρL=676.695; ρV=15.381 kg/m³.
interpretation: K must be selected for service/vendor and de-rated at high pressure where applicable.
verification: Square-root term dimensionless; result units m/s.
assumptions: Hydraulic screen, not certified separator design.

title: Hydraulic minimum area and diameter
purpose: Convert vapour flow/capacity velocity to minimum gross area and equivalent diameter.
interpretation: This is a hydraulic lower bound before practical allowances.
verification: Area and diameter relationship dimensionally consistent.
assumptions: K and gas density are not final design data.

title: Practical preliminary diameter selection
purpose: Select a manufacturable screening geometry above hydraulic minimum.
data: Dmin≈0.2726 m; selected D=0.500 m for practical geometry; length assumption 2.0 m.
interpretation: The selected diameter provides greater gas area and a vessel volume above the 0.3 m³ lower bound of one cited ambient-pressure cost correlation.
verification: Actual gas superficial velocity is recalculated next.
assumptions: Practical screening choice, not final design or mechanical code selection.

title: Actual gas superficial velocity at selected diameter
purpose: Recalculate gas velocity at selected diameter and capacity margin.
interpretation: The selected D reduces velocity substantially relative to the preliminary capacity ceiling.
assumptions: No allowance for inlet jet, foaming, droplet size or internals blocking area.

title: Liquid hold-up and working level
purpose: Calculate 180 s liquid hold-up at selected diameter.
interpretation: This is a theoretical liquid depth, excluding surge/freeboard, heads, internals, low/high-level separation and instrument requirements.
assumptions: Residence time is assumed, not site- or service-approved.

title: Vapour nozzle preliminary bore
purpose: Estimate vapor nozzle bore from assumed velocity.
data: VdotV=0.0421004 m³/s; assumed nozzle velocity 15 m/s.
interpretation: A nominal 65 mm nozzle might be considered for preliminary layout.
assumptions: Not a pipe code selection; pressure drop, noise, reinforcement, schedule and corrosion not evaluated.

title: Liquid nozzle preliminary bore
purpose: Estimate liquid nozzle bore from assumed velocity.
data: Q_L=0.000358380 m³/s; assumed liquid nozzle velocity 1 m/s.
interpretation: A nominal 25 mm nozzle could be a layout placeholder.
assumptions: Must check minimum practical line size, drainage, flashing, controls and pressure drop.

title: Illustrative pressure wall-thickness check
purpose: Demonstrate a pressure-wall equation with explicit unapproved assumptions.
data: Pdesign=1.8 MPa; D=0.5 m (R=250 mm); assumed S=115 MPa; E=0.85; CA=1.5 mm.
interpretation: This demonstrates equation handling only. Material allowable stress, code edition, weld category, design temperature, heads, nozzles, cyclic loading and fabrication minima are not frozen.
verification: Units in numerator and denominator reduce to mm.
assumptions: NOT ASME DESIGN / NOT FOR FABRICATION. Replace S/E/CA/design pressure from approved code basis.

title: Water sensible heat duty
purpose: Integrate NIST Shomate liquid-water Cp from assumed feed T to separator T.
data: T1=425.1253 K, T2=445.1253 K; F_water=50,000 mol/h. NIST Shomate coefficients as register.
substitution: Numerical quadrature of NIST expression over 425.1253-445.1253 K gives integral 1565.126 J/mol; Q=50000×1565.126/1000
interpretation: Sensible heating contribution for the water feed under the assumed feed/outlet thermal path.
verification: Quadrature reproduces integrated Cp; correlation valid 298-500 K.
assumptions: Energy path assumes liquid feed heated by 20 K before flash; ignores pressure enthalpy effects and mixing excess enthalpy.

title: Ethanol sensible heat duty
purpose: Estimate sensible heating using an explicit assumed mean liquid heat capacity.
data: F_E=50,000 mol/h; Cp_E assumed 130 J/mol/K; ΔT=20 K.
interpretation: Contributes 36.11 kW.
assumptions: 130 J/mol/K is an engineering assumption; NIST value 112.4 J/mol/K at 298.15K is below the calculation interval and cannot be directly treated as measured at 435K.

title: Ethanol latent heat
purpose: Calculate ethanol latent heat from NIST critical scaling correlation.
interpretation: The correlation provides a pure-fluid saturation latent heat for a screening estimate.
verification: T=445.125 K is within 298-469 K range.
assumptions: Mixture-phase enthalpy is not the same as pure saturation latent heat at system pressure.

title: Water latent heat screening
purpose: Estimate water latent heat using Watson scaling from normal boiling point.
interpretation: This is an estimate for a pure fluid and is retained only as a duty screening assumption.
verification: Correlation form is dimensionless ratio scaling.
assumptions: Replace with consistent water/steam and mixture enthalpy calculations from IAPWS plus validated mixture thermodynamics.

title: Illustrative total duty
purpose: Combine sensible and latent contributions to obtain a preliminary thermal load.
interpretation: This is a scenario estimate, not a closed thermodynamic energy balance. It ignores mixture excess enthalpy and EOS departure enthalpy.
assumptions: Do not use for heat exchanger design, utility procurement or plant guarantee.

title: Duty sensitivity to ethanol Cp assumption
purpose: Quantify the duty effect of uncertainty in ethanol liquid Cp.
data: Cp_E scenarios = 115,130,145,160 J/mol/K; other terms fixed from MC-041/043/044.
substitution: Recompute Q at each Cp; no refit of VLE.
interpretation: Changing the assumed Cp by ±15 around 130 J/mol/K changes total duty by about ±4.17 kW, much less than unquantified latent/excess enthalpy uncertainty.
assumptions: One-factor screen, not full uncertainty propagation.

title: Steam consumption scenario
purpose: Convert illustrative duty to steam demand using assumed latent enthalpy.
data: Q=2,392,715.821 kJ/h; steam Δh assumed 1890 kJ/kg (not computed by IAPWS).
interpretation: This is an order-of-magnitude steam scenario only.
verification: kJ/h divided by kJ/kg produces kg/h.
assumptions: Use IAPWS-IF97 enthalpy difference for actual steam condition and condensate return state.

title: Annual steam cost scenario
purpose: Illustrate OPEX dependence on tariff without implying a market quotation.
data: msteam=1265.99 kg/h; 8000 h/y assumed; tariff scenarios 15,25,40 USD/t.
substitution: Annual steam≈10127.9 t/y; multiply by each scenario tariff.
result: USD/y scenarios generated in utility cost CSV.
interpretation: Tariff and operating hours are scenario assumptions.
assumptions: Not an accepted OPEX because duty and tariff are not approved.

title: CEPCI escalation factor
purpose: Demonstrate cost index escalation from 2019 average to June 2024 preliminary index.
interpretation: A historical cost may be escalated by approximately 31.49% over the stated index interval, if scope and index application are appropriate.
assumptions: No 2025/2026 value is invented; cost correlation applicability and pressure factors remain separate.

title: Literature model-comparison deviation
purpose: Compare published azeotrope predictions with the experiment at 1.5 MPa.
data: Experimental xaz=.857, Taz=440.70 K; PRSV x=.883,T=441.09 K; PRSV-WS x=.864,T=440.83 K.
result: PRSV-WS has lower published azeotrope deviations in this comparison.
interpretation: This compares literature-reported calculations, not a reproduction in this project.
assumptions: No claim that the target NRTL-SRK model has been independently fitted or benchmarked.

title: Base fugacity residual acceptance ratio
purpose: Measure how far the target model misses the residual threshold.
interpretation: The empirical tie-line fails the model acceptance gate by about five orders of magnitude.
assumptions: Diagnostic at reference tie-line, not model prediction deviation.

title: Azeotrope pressure trend
purpose: Summarize published high-pressure azeotrope changes.
equation: Δxaz and ΔTaz between cited pressure points
interpretation: The pressure trend motivates a high-pressure model and forbids applying low-pressure parameters without checking.
verification: Values are from published experimental summary.
assumptions: Only three discrete pressures; do not interpolate process-wide behaviour as validated.

title: Uncertainty propagation boundary for tie-line β
purpose: Assess what can be quantified from reported composition uncertainties.
data: Paper reports y uncertainty ±0.004 and T uncertainty ±0.4 K in source text; x uncertainty not extracted/established.
substitution: At base, ∂β/∂x and ∂β/∂y evaluate from x,y,z; propagate y-only ±0.004 separately, do not construct full combined uncertainty.
result: Full β uncertainty BLOCKED because numeric x uncertainty is unavailable; y-only perturbation saved in uncertainty CSV.
interpretation: A fully numeric combined interval would imply an unsupported x uncertainty.
verification: Partial sensitivity is explicitly distinguished from full uncertainty.
assumptions: Coverage factor for reported uncertainty not independently confirmed; preserve source wording.

title: Component ordering check
purpose: Ensure all property, parameter and stream arrays use ethanol=1 and water=2.
data: Configuration, reference table and NRTL/SRK arrays.
substitution: Cross-check each CSV header, config component list and parameter labels.
interpretation: Swapping components silently would change NRTL τ direction and reported product composition.
verification: Static audit record plus MATLAB input test planned.
assumptions: MATLAB tests unexecuted until runtime available.

title: Energy sign convention
purpose: Establish sign convention for a steady-state control volume.
data: Steady state; no reaction; assumed no shaft work in reference calculation.
equation: F h_in + Qdot = Σ_out n h_out + Wdot; Qdot positive into process, Wdot positive work out of control volume as assignment form indicates.
substitution: Do not numerically solve Qdot from EOS until a consistent enthalpy datum and excess/departure terms are implemented.
result: Qdot ACCEPTED VALUE NOT CALCULATED; screen = 664.643 kW scenario only.
interpretation: This keeps a physically defensible boundary between the screening duty and an energy-closure result.
verification: Equation and sign convention are documented for future implementation.
assumptions: The screen uses pure-fluid latent properties and one assumed Cp.

title: Vessel volume and cost-correlation validity
purpose: Check whether geometry falls within cited reference correlation range.
data: D=0.5 m, straight length=2.0m; Turton/OpenPyTEA vertical-vessel volume correlation nominal range 0.3-520 m³, ambient pressure, CS purchased cost.
equation: V=πD²L/4; compare V against 0.3m³ lower bound.
result: Volume is nominally within size range, but cost correlation is ambient-pressure basis and requires pressure/material correction.
interpretation: Only base correlation domain is met. Industrial CAPEX remains blocked because pressure rating, metallurgy and installed factors are unresolved.
assumptions: Do not treat an ambient-pressure purchase correlation as the high-pressure installed cost.

title: Souders-Brown margin vs diameter
purpose: Show how selected diameter changes superficial gas velocity.
result: The larger screening diameter reduces velocity by about 64%.
interpretation: Geometry is an important hydraulic sensitivity and should be optimized using validated loads and internals data.
assumptions: Hydraulic screen only.

title: Feed throughput effect on equipment load
purpose: Scale phase rates and approximate vapour volume with throughput.
data: Base V=69.8046 kmol/h; qv=.0421004m³/s at F=100 kmol/h.
result: Loads scale linearly under fixed intensive state.
interpretation: Higher throughput may require larger diameter; the linear scaling is a first estimate.
assumptions: No scale-dependent entrainment effects accounted for.

title: NIST Antoine correlation validity check
purpose: Verify both vapor pressure equations are evaluated within stated temperature ranges.
interpretation: Correlation validity is a necessary condition, not enough to guarantee mixture-model validity.
assumptions: NIST data source and unit basis recorded in property register.

title: Alternative model comparison hierarchy
purpose: Interpret comparative literature data in correct evidence class.
data: Experimental azeotrope and PRSV/PRSV-WS reported values at 1500 kPa.
substitution: Keep source-model outputs as publisher-reported; do not substitute them for local reimplementation.
result: PRSV-WS literature comparison has smaller absolute azeotrope deviations in this study.
interpretation: The target alternative for code benchmarking can be PRSV-WS only after its parameter/mixing-rule convention and implementation are sourced.
assumptions: Alternative model not implemented in current MATLAB package.
